mystery_1_fashion_drawing.location: page 14 of the manual, Illustration No. 11 (corrected 25 Sept 2026: not 'No. 13' -- the manual page itself, read directly, plainly reads 'Illustration No. 11'; signed 'Mary Helen Shaw')

mystery_1_fashion_drawing.encoding_hypothesis_a: the manual's own caption (Illustration No. 11's introduction, page 14) says: 'a system of Morse (not the usual dot and dash) has been introduced into the embroidery, etc., of the dresses' -- i.e. explicitly NOT classic dot/dash Morse shapes; the specific graphical encoding is what is unsolved
mystery_1_fashion_drawing.known_plaintext_part_b: 'Before Arras' -- ENGLISH ONLY in the manual's own caption; no German given by the manual for this part either. 'Vor Arras' remains only Schmeh's own guess (Arras = a town in northern France)
mystery_1_fashion_drawing.encoding_hypothesis_b: per the manual, hidden in the drawing's signature, written in French shorthand -- the specific shorthand system and how it renders 'Before Arras' is unsolved; dbourdeau/cyphersolver's repo (15 Sept 2026, found 25 Sept 2026) favours Duployé over the blog's earlier German-Stolze-Schrey guess, unverified at available resolution

mystery_2_map.location: page 17 of the manual, Illustration No. 14 (page 16's text: 'Morse can be introduced into the heavy lining in the print such as tram lines, etc.')
mystery_2_map.known_plaintext: 'Oil has arrived, everything is ready. Gustav available for the appointed day.' -- the manual's own caption says this is a translation ('The message in German when translated read:--') but gives ENGLISH ONLY, no German original anywhere in the pages read (corrected 25 Sept 2026); Schmeh's blog German back-translation ('Öl ist angekommen...') remains only his own guess.
mystery_2_map.encoding_hypothesis: manual's own caption: 'The morse letters had to be transposed 11 positions forward' -- confirmed by a 2016 blog commenter's fragment AATHUT -> (+11) -> LLESFE, part of ALLES FERTIG ('everything is ready'); the marks themselves (which map feature = dot, which = dash) are unresolved. dbourdeau/cyphersolver's repo (15 Sept 2026) ruled out the tram-band ink runs themselves (ordinary printed fill, no two-length structure) and located the real carrier as small pen marks added beside the Raadhuisstraat band -- blocked on resolution, same as mystery 1.

Cost $1-2. Test the Gustav map (mystery 2) analogously once its own encoding hypothesis is confirmed from the fetched manual text (test 1).
